title: Customer Payment Card — Settling an Energy Monitoring & Performance Subscription in One Payment
content:
# Settling a Subscription in One Payment

Payment card for the request, under Energy Monitoring & Performance Subscriptions, of a building owner who asks to clear their subscription in a single payment.

## The request and the quoted sum

A building owner who asks to settle an energy monitoring subscription in one payment is quoted the sum that clears it, and that sum is worked out from the subscription's own ledger rather than from the balance the dashboard displays. The sum is entered as one payment applied to the oldest invoice standing unpaid on the subscription, whatever else it clears.

The sum the owner settles is fixed only after the charge owed for the analyst hours drawn beyond the year's included pool stands invoiced on the subscription.

## How the payment is made

`settle_subscription_balance_535836bf` is the building owner's own tool: the client services agent unlocks it and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it, paying money into the subscription account with the payment recorded against the invoice they name. It is entered on the subscription's payment history with the day it was received and reduces the amount the subscription owes by the amount paid; the owner sees it on the account and on the next statement. The same payment entered twice with the same details lands once.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `subscription_id` | the reference number of the energy monitoring subscription the payment is entered on, as the client services agent states it when handing the payment over | Id |
| `customer_id` | the reference number of the building owner's account making the payment, as the client services agent states it when handing the payment over | Id |
| `invoice_ref` | the invoice number the payment is applied to, copied from the invoice history of this subscription | exactly INV- followed by 8 digits; never left empty |
| `payment_method` | how the money is being paid, one of exactly four values | `check`, `ach`, `credit_card`, `wire` |
| `amount_usd` | the money amount paid in USD | positive, 2 decimal places, rounded half up to the cent as it is entered |

The four payment methods are: `check` — the owner is posting or hand-delivering a paper cheque drawn on their own bank; `ach` — the owner authorises an electronic debit from the bank account already held on their file; `credit_card` — the owner is paying on a company card taken over the phone; `wire` — the owner is sending a same-day bank wire transfer from their treasury.

## Return

A confirmation sentence in plain text naming the subscription the payment was entered on, the invoice number it was applied to, the amount taken in USD to two decimal places and the way it was paid. Any sentence of that shape means the payment now stands on the subscription's payment history. No other return is defined.
